question: How does Raymond James's affiliation-choice model work commercially?

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Raymond James refers to its multiple affiliation options as AdvisorChoice®, under which financial advisors affiliate directly as either employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers serviced through the RIA and Custody Services division (FY2025).

Raymond James Financial: The affiliation options listed by Raymond James include Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA (page content as of 2026-04-21).

Raymond James Financial: Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff, serve predominantly retail clients, and are compensated primarily through a payout on the revenues they generate, also participating in the firm's employee benefit plans (FY2025).

Raymond James Financial: Under the Traditional Employee model, advisors receive up to a 50% payout plus a full array of competitive employee benefits, with minimum 5 years of experience required (page content as of 2026-04-21).

Raymond James Financial: Under the Advisor Select model, advisors receive a 70-80% gross payout plus a full array of competitive employee benefits, and run their own branch (an employee affiliation option for advisors who want to lead a team) (page content as of 2026-04-21).

Raymond James Financial: Under the Independent Contractor model, advisors receive an 81% to 90% payout, and leverage Raymond James' third-party partnerships to build their own benefits package (page content as of 2026-04-21).

Raymond James Financial: Independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors (FY2025).

Raymond James Financial: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), management said independent payouts are higher than employee payouts because independent advisors cover their own overhead costs, real estate, health insurance, etc.; the employee side uses tiered payout systems where higher production moves an advisor up the payout grid.

Raymond James Financial: Independent contractor financial advisors may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division, and with specific approval may conduct certain other approved business activities such as insurance products, independent RIA services, and accounting and tax services (FY2025).

Raymond James Financial: On the 4Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management said Raymond James is agnostic about how an advisor affiliates (employee vs independent contractor vs RIA custody), wanting advisors to choose based on fit with its culture, values, platform and capabilities.

Raymond James Financial: The affiliation spectrum ranges from employee (RJA) to independent contractor (ICD) to RIA & Custody Services, described by Raymond James as servicing the largest addressable market in the industry (Investor Day deck, June 2025).

Raymond James Financial: How the affiliation-choice model works commercially (payouts, fees, economics by affiliation type): Under the Bank & Credit Union model, advisors receive a competitive compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James (page content as of 2026-04-21).
Raymond James Financial: Under the Corporate RIA model, advisors receive an 81% to 90% payout and build their own benefits package through third-party partnerships (page content as of 2026-04-21).

Raymond James Financial: Under the RIA & Custody Services model, advisors work with their RIA or broker/dealer to determine compensation and create their own benefits package (page content as of 2026-04-21).

Raymond James Financial: On the 4Q24 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2024), management said that for RIA custody, the margin on a P&L basis is actually higher because the attachment revenue booked is much lower, whereas in other businesses Raymond James grosses up the revenues pre-payout; ROCA varies with the RIA's asset mix and pricing structure.
Raymond James Financial: For firms affiliated through the RIA and Custody Services division, revenues related to their assets in the PCG segment are included in Account and service fees (FY2025).
Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2025, Raymond James reported 8,943 total financial advisors, consisting of 3,878 employee financial advisors and 5,065 independent contractor advisors.
Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2024, Raymond James reported 8,787 total financial advisors, consisting of 3,826 employees and 4,961 independent contractors.
Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2023, Raymond James reported 8,712 total financial advisors, consisting of 3,693 employees and 5,019 independent contractors.

Raymond James Financial: On the fiscal 4Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management said Raymond James ended fiscal 2025 with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year, reflecting solid advisor retention and strong recruiting results.

Raymond James Financial: For fiscal 2025 (domestic independent contractor and employee channels), Raymond James reported record trailing 12-month production for recruited financial advisors of $407 million.

Raymond James Financial: Through the first 9 months of fiscal 2026, Raymond James recruited advisors with trailing 12-month production totaling $393 million (domestic independent contractor and employee channels).

Raymond James Financial: In the fiscal third quarter (period ended June 30, 2026), Raymond James recruited financial advisors to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing 12-month production totaling $156 million.

Raymond James Financial: In the fiscal second quarter (period ended March 31, 2026), Raymond James recruited financial advisors to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing 12-month production totaling $141 million, the second-highest quarterly result in its history.
Raymond James Financial: For the year ended September 30, 2025, Raymond James's domestic financial advisor retention remained very strong.

Raymond James Financial: On the 4Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James reports a 97% advisor satisfaction rate with its surveys, which he described as the best he knows of in the industry, and cited this retention as the foundation for growth.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James defines domestic Private Client Group net new assets as domestic Private Client Group client inflows, including dividends and interest, less domestic Private Client Group client outflows, including commissions, advisory fees, and other fees.

Raymond James Financial: On the 4Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management stated Raymond James does not lead with the highest transition check but leads with culture and capabilities, requiring competitive economics while offering a differentiated value proposition, and remaining disciplined on transition assistance and advisor economics.

Raymond James Financial: On the fiscal 4Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management stated the firm is focused on the long term and providing a stable platform, attracting and retaining advisors with unique culture, leading service and robust platform rather than the largest check.

Raymond James Financial: On the fiscal 4Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management stated Raymond James values independence to foster an environment where advisors can provide objective advice, unlike competitors that change comp plans each year to cross-sell bank products.

Raymond James Financial: On the 4Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management stated the firm has the largest addressable market in the industry because it offers all affiliation options and is agnostic about how advisors affiliate, wanting them drawn to its culture, values, platform and capabilities.

Raymond James Financial: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), management stated advisors do not have to choose between culture and capabilities, offering a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology, products and solutions.

Raymond James Financial: On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), management stated the firm has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options (employee to independent contractor to RIA custody) with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them.

Raymond James Financial: On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), management described advisor recruiting as a long-term marathon, not a sprint, targeting advisors who want to stay long-term rather than those moving for the highest check.

Raymond James Financial: On the 4Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management stated consistency is a critical concept in recruiting and retaining advisors, focusing on finding advisors who are good cultural fits across affiliation options.

Raymond James Financial: On the 1Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2024), management described a 'best of both worlds' value proposition combining scope and breadth of products and capabilities with a culture anchored on putting people first.

Raymond James Financial: On the fiscal 4Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management stated its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

Raymond James Financial: Trade press reports that management stated the advisor, not the home office, is the client, and that the firm builds its advisory ranks through individualized recruitment rather than large-scale acquisitions, evaluating each prospective advisor one-on-one (published September 2026).
